prompt: The book cover of "The Ravens" by Tomas Bannerhed employs a minimalist yet striking design. Dominating the composition is a large, sweeping black brushstroke, textured to appear as both dynamic motion and a looming presence. Emerging from the upper curve of the stroke is a solitary raven, wings outstretched as if in mid-flight, symbolizing freedom or an ominous foreboding. The surrounding white space accentuates the contrast of the dark elements, giving the design a stark and raw energy. The title, "THE RAVENS," is presented in a hand-drawn, uneven font, resembling scratches or etchings, further amplifying the sense of unease and nature's primal forces. Ink splatters and scattered dots surround the brushstroke and text, suggesting chaos, unpredictability, or even violence. Beneath the title, the author's name, Tomas Bannerhed, is written in clean, serifed capital letters, grounding the design with a sense of order amid the chaos above. The overall aesthetic captures a blend of naturalism and the abstract, hinting at themes of mystery, nature, and existential reflection. The monochrome palette heightens the emotional intensity, drawing the viewer into the stark and haunting atmosphere of the story. --ar 2:3 --style raw --profile yfqg331 --v 6.1
